task.name: Run artifacts are published once per sprint but the gate that requires them committed runs once per story, so every story after the first is refused
task.story_text:
## Observed

A sprint writes each story's canonical run record to `.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json`
and its knowledge summary to `.forge/knowledge/summaries/<run_id>.yaml` as that story
completes. Both paths are tracked: forge's own generated `.gitignore` denies `.forge/**`
and then explicitly re-includes them as project memory.

Those files are committed once, by the audit publish step that runs after every story
in the sprint has finished.

Between those two points the landing precondition is evaluated at each story's entry.
Under a landing workflow it refuses any story when the project root has uncommitted
changes, untracked files included. The first story's own run record is such a file, so
the second story is refused before dispatch, and the refusal writes a further run record,
so the third story is refused naming two files, and so on. A three-story sprint completes
one story and refuses the rest; the commit that would have cleared the condition runs
after the last refusal.

Observed on 0.15.0rc7, sprint `db58df9c0430`, stories issue-337 (DONE, $23.87),
issue-339 and issue-340 (both ESCALATE at workspace entry, 0.35s and 0.30s, no agents
dispatched).

#2546 described this same refusal as a consequence it was closing, and extended the
publish step to cover knowledge summaries as well as audit records. That widened which
artifacts the end-of-sprint commit includes; it did not change when the commit happens,
so the refusal survives the fix.

## Expected

Where a process both produces an artifact into a tracked location and enforces a
precondition that the tracked location be clean, the publishing of that artifact keeps
pace with the enforcement rather than lagging it. An artifact a run creates as part of
its normal success is not left in a state that refuses the run's own successor.

This is not a matter of exempting the artifact from the check. The records are the
product of the compounding-memory feature, not scratch output: they exist to be
committed, shared, and read by later runs, so the condition the gate observes is real
and the gate is correct to observe it. What is wrong is that forge leaves it standing
across the window in which it will refuse itself.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `ea85f87c1f538f2bf97acd55992fbb81bcc5a3bb` captured at `2026-08-20T05:42:25.832044+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/sprint/audit_publish.py` — `sha256:90e6a54a2d1e792ddcf118553f129559764f4a830a5d5aaafc5379fa0fdf42a1`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py` — `sha256:9c5ed787de305cccfaf0be7043a5e46d33aae7d1dc98f2edc57bc9609516d2ae`
- `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` — `sha256:bfa6ea79a1dbf80cd9fb15e4400e65fbf032b14c5efb38e821065dd543843cf7`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py` — `sha256:50e5d5f16325057a457d662ee3578caf9bb083fdd60d955edffd43a27f0ad062`
- `src/theforge/sprint/audit.py` — `sha256:21dde7dc67365593210f08b7c08866a02efb633b127a6fa22e206a4ca756c57a`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/knowledge_summary_flow.py` — `sha256:ced51015f310c289c1ec51be5eb12a819a1cdff980a0ed9587ecec78bb38a423`
- `src/theforge/knowledge_summary.py` — `sha256:ee958a8d065137b01e527f92f42a271a88b28871b5d9ee5f67ee9948361273d0`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/audit_storage.py` — `sha256:23bae69bf94a7366bd00c90504faff4aee5410c6dd1f4e85e7e94967db1e3c0b`
- `src/theforge/knowledge_index.py` — `sha256:a5d22f42fa75e82af4bae8905d97b173c7e90cdf3814589d507ee357592888f0`

### Observed symptom

In a multi-story sprint that lands stories into the project-root checkout, only the
first story runs; every subsequent story is refused at workspace entry with
"LANDING PRECONDITION: uncommitted changes in project root", naming the previous
story's own audit/knowledge-summary files as the dirt, even though those files were
produced by forge's own successful completion of the prior story.

### Reproduction / evidence

Code inspection confirms the full causal chain at HEAD (release/v0.15):

1. Per-story write, happens once per story, into the shared project-root checkout:
   `src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1616` and `:1618` call
   `_write_native_story_record(config.project_root, audit_data, ...)`, which
   (audit.py:296-339) writes `.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json` directly under
   `config.project_root` — the base-branch checkout, not the story's worktree.
   `knowledge_summary_flow.maybe_generate_run_summary` (invoked at audit.py:1617)
   similarly writes `.forge/knowledge/summaries/<run_id>.yaml` there (per
   `src/theforge/coordinator/knowledge_summary_flow.py:136`, which reads back
   `config.project_root / ".forge" / "audits" / "runs" / f"{run_id}.json"`).
   This runs at the end of *each* story, inside the sprint's per-story loop in
   `run_sprint` (`src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:4606`+, calling `run_task`).

2. Per-story precondition, evaluated at every story's entry, against that same
   checkout: `landing_precondition_error` (`src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:417`)
   calls `project_root_dirty_status` (`workspace.py:378`, `git status --porcelain`)
   and refuses on any dirt, untracked files included. It is invoked at
   `src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:1179` (WORKSPACE phase entry) and
   `engine.py:1687` (resume entry) for every story — not just the sprint's first.

3. Sprint-terminal commit, happens exactly once, after the whole story loop:
   `publish_story_run_audits` is called at `src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:8204`,
   immediately after `write_terminal_sprint_audits` (`runner.py:8186`), both after
   the sprint's story-dispatch loop has fully finished. `_commit_story_run_audits`
   (`src/theforge/sprint/audit_publish.py:178-259`) is the only place that commits
   `.forge/audits/runs` and `.forge/knowledge/summaries`.

So story 1 completes and leaves untracked/modified files under
`.forge/audits/runs/` and `.forge/knowledge/summaries/` in the project root; story
2's WORKSPACE-entry `landing_precondition_error` check (engine.py:1179) sees that
dirt and escalates before any agent is dispatched; story 2's own escalation writes
a further run record, so story 3 is refused naming two files; and so on. The commit
that would clear the condition (audit_publish.py) does not run until after the last
story has already been refused.

This matches the reported sprint `db58df9c0430` (story 1 issue-337 DONE $23.87;
stories issue-339/issue-340 ESCALATE at 0.35s/0.30s with zero agents dispatched —
consistent with a WORKSPACE-phase refusal that fires before dev/review spend).

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** #2546's extension of the publish step to cover knowledge summaries changed WHEN artifacts are committed, so the bug should already be fixed.
  - Evidence: audit_publish.py's _STORY_RUN_ARTIFACT_DIRS now includes both dirs (confirming #2546 widened scope), but _commit_story_run_audits is still only invoked once, from publish_story_run_audits at runner.py:8204, which itself is called once after the entire sprint's story loop (runner.py:8183-8204 sits after all per-story dispatch). #2546 changed *what* gets committed, not *when* — the timing defect the issue describes is unchanged.
- **[ruled out]** The per-story audit/summary artifacts are written into each story's isolated worktree, not the shared project-root checkout, so they shouldn't collide with the landing precondition at all.
  - Evidence: _write_native_story_record is called with config.project_root (audit.py:1616/1618), and knowledge_summary_flow.py:136 reads back from config.project_root / '.forge' / 'audits' / 'runs' — both explicitly target the shared base-branch checkout, the same path project_root_dirty_status/landing_precondition_error inspect (workspace.py:378-455).
- **[confirmed]** The landing precondition and the per-story artifact writer are the same mechanism operating correctly by design; the mismatch is that artifact publication (commit) is sprint-terminal while the precondition check is per-story-entry.
  - Evidence: Direct code citations above: writer runs once per story (audit.py:1616/1618, inside the per-story loop reached via run_task), precondition check runs at every story's WORKSPACE/resume entry (engine.py:1179, engine.py:1687), and the only commit of these paths happens once, after the full story loop (runner.py:8183-8204).

### Confirmed cause

The story-run audit record (`.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json`) and knowledge
summary (`.forge/knowledge/summaries/<run_id>.yaml`) are written into the shared
project-root checkout at the end of every story (`_write_native_story_record` /
`maybe_generate_run_summary`, called from `src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1616-1618`
during each story's completion inside the sprint's per-story loop). The commit that
publishes those tracked paths to the base branch (`_commit_story_run_audits`, via
`publish_story_run_audits`) runs only once, after the sprint's entire story-dispatch
loop has finished (`src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:8183-8204`). The landing
precondition (`landing_precondition_error` / `project_root_dirty_status` in
`src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py`) is evaluated at every story's entry
(`src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:1179` and `:1687`) and refuses on any dirt in
the project root, untracked files included. Because publication lags every
per-story write by the length of the whole sprint, story 2 onward finds the prior
story's own uncommitted artifacts in the project root and is refused before
dispatch — a self-inflicted refusal, not an operator-caused one.

### Affected code path

- src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1590-1618 (`_write_native_story_record` calls,
  per-story write into `config.project_root`)
- src/theforge/sprint/audit_publish.py:178-259 (`_commit_story_run_audits`) and
  :450-480 (`publish_story_run_audits`) — the only commit point, sprint-terminal
- src/theforge/sprint/runner.py:8183-8204 (call site of
  `write_terminal_sprint_audits` / `publish_story_run_audits`, after the
  per-story dispatch loop)
- src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py:417-455 (`landing_precondition_error`,
  the per-story-entry check that observes the lag)
- src/theforge/coordinator/engine.py:1179, :1687 (per-story invocation points of
  the precondition check)

### Fix-success criterion

In a multi-story sprint where every story lands into the project-root checkout, a
story that completes and leaves only its own canonical run-record/knowledge-summary
artifacts as project-root dirt does not cause the next story's landing-precondition
check to refuse. Concretely: a sprint of N ≥ 2 independent stories, run under a
workflow with `on_approve: merge` (or `--auto-merge`), completes all N stories
without any ESCALATE whose message is the "LANDING PRECONDITION: uncommitted
changes" string citing `.forge/audits/runs/` or `.forge/knowledge/summaries/`
paths as the dirt. A precondition refusal caused by genuine operator-introduced
dirt (unrelated files) must still fire.

### Notes

Root cause is a timing/ordering mismatch between two correct-in-isolation
mechanisms (write-per-story vs. commit-once-per-sprint vs. check-per-story-entry),
not a bug in either mechanism's own logic. The issue text is explicit that the fix
is not to exempt these artifacts from the precondition — the condition being
observed is real. A fix implementer has design freedom on where to close the gap
(e.g., commit/publish these artifact dirs immediately after each story rather than
once at sprint end), but that decision is intentionally left open here per the
issue's "Expected" section, which states the requirement (publication keeps pace
with enforcement) without prescribing the mechanism.

handoff.summary: Closed the timing gap between per-story artifact writes and the once-per-sprint publish. Added publish_pending_story_run_audits() to sprint/audit_publish.py — the same publish path as the terminal one (same branch check, dirty-dir scoping, push/reconcile retry, local-only handling, publish-state recording) but with a failure logged and deferred rather than raised, so a transport fault mid-run cannot abandon the stories still to come. The sprint scheduler calls it at the top of each loop pass that has ready work and no workers in flight: the `for task in ready` body below is the sole place a slug is registered active, so no story can enter WORKSPACE between a completed story's artifact write and the publish, and the previous pass has already settled every terminal audit write including the post-integration force_replace rewrite. It is skipped while workers are in flight because those workers merge into the same checkout under a landing workflow (taking the index out from under a merge would turn bookkeeping into a story failure) and because publishing there would not be sufficient anyway — a sibling finishing after the publish re-dirties the root before the next entry. The sprint-terminal publish_story_run_audits call is unchanged and remains the final, fatal, idempotent sweep.

deferred_items: Parallel sprints (max_parallel > 1) under a project-root landing workflow keep today's behaviour: the mid-loop publish is skipped while workers are in flight. This is deliberate and documented at the call site — publishing there would race a worker's merge on the same git index, and would not be sufficient regardless, since a sibling finishing after the publish re-dirties the root before the next story's entry. Making parallel dispatch race-free would need a different mechanism (e.g. a project-root git lock shared by the publish and _merge_branch), which is outside this story's scope. The reported failure is sequential and is fully closed.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (parallel sprints) — carried in part. publish_story_run_audits re-raises StoryRunAuditPublishError on branch-check, commit, push, or reconcile failure (audit_publish.py:466-480); today that only ever happens once, at sprint exit. Called mid-loop, the same raise would abort a sprint that has already completed stories, converting a publish-transport problem into lost remaining work. The plan does not say what the mid-loop call does with that exception.
  Suggestion: Decide explicitly in Step 2: either wrap the mid-loop call so a failure is logged and deferred to the terminal sweep (which still raises), or document that mid-loop failure is intentionally fatal. Add a test asserting the chosen behaviour.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (publish before the landing-status rewrite) is only partly retired. src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1605-1618 documents that a sprint calls this writer more than once for the same finished story (pending integration, landing, wrap-up), and _write_native_story_record is invoked again with force_replace=True. Any rewrite that lands after the per-story publish but before the next story's WORKSPACE entry re-dirties .forge/audits/runs/ and reproduces the refusal. The plan lists the call sites to cover but does not establish that the last rewrite for a story always precedes the publish on that pass.
  Suggestion: In Step 2, place the publish strictly after the final force_replace rewrite for each story that the current scheduler pass performs, and cover the pending-integration/queued-PR case in the Step 3 regression by rewriting the run record after completion and asserting the next entry still sees a clean project root.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Ordering guarantee for concurrent dispatch is asserted but not mechanically pinned. Step 2 says the publish happens 'before the loop can dispatch more ready work', which is what keeps a later worker's WORKSPACE entry (engine.py:1179) from racing the publish; the plan's test in Step 3 is described as a sequential landing regression only.
  Suggestion: Add an assertion (or ordering-sensitive fake, in the style of test_publisher_may_take_phase_lock_without_deadlocking) that no story dispatch occurs between a completed story's artifact write and the publish call on that scheduler pass.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 3 (auto_push off for local-merge runs) is retired as stated: publish_story_run_audits already routes publish= through _base_branch_tracks_origin (audit_publish.py:465), and _commit_story_run_audits still commits locally when publish is false, which is enough to clean the working tree for the next precondition check. Worth one explicit test rather than relying on the existing terminal-path coverage.
  Suggestion: Extend Step 1's tests with a lands_locally / auto_push-off case asserting a local-only commit still clears project_root_dirty_status.

plan_finding_registry.description: Risk 1 (parallel sprints) — carried in part. publish_story_run_audits re-raises StoryRunAuditPublishError on branch-check, commit, push, or reconcile failure (audit_publish.py:466-480); today that only ever happens once, at sprint exit. Called mid-loop, the same raise would abort a sprint that has already completed stories, converting a publish-transport problem into lost remaining work. The plan does not say what the mid-loop call does with that exception.

Risk 2 (publish before the landing-status rewrite) is only partly retired. src/theforge/sprint/audit.py:1605-1618 documents that a sprint calls this writer more than once for the same finished story (pending integration, landing, wrap-up), and _write_native_story_record is invoked again with force_replace=True. Any rewrite that lands after the per-story publish but before the next story's WORKSPACE entry re-dirties .forge/audits/runs/ and reproduces the refusal. The plan lists the call sites to cover but does not establish that the last rewrite for a story always precedes the publish on that pass.

Ordering guarantee for concurrent dispatch is asserted but not mechanically pinned. Step 2 says the publish happens 'before the loop can dispatch more ready work', which is what keeps a later worker's WORKSPACE entry (engine.py:1179) from racing the publish; the plan's test in Step 3 is described as a sequential landing regression only.

Risk 3 (auto_push off for local-merge runs) is retired as stated: publish_story_run_audits already routes publish= through _base_branch_tracks_origin (audit_publish.py:465), and _commit_story_run_audits still commits locally when publish is false, which is enough to clean the working tree for the next precondition check. Worth one explicit test rather than relying on the existing terminal-path coverage.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Publish pending canonical story-run artifacts during sprint execution immediately after a story's terminal audit state is written, while keeping the existing sprint-terminal publish as an idempotent final sweep. Do not change the landing precondition or exempt `.forge` paths; make the tracked artifact dirs clean before any later story can enter WORKSPACE.

steps.description: Make audit artifact publishing explicitly safe to call more than once per sprint.
steps.details: Keep `_commit_story_run_audits` and `publish_story_run_audits` as the single publish path for `.forge/audits/runs` and `.forge/knowledge/summaries`. Preserve the current branch check, dirty-dir scoping, push/reconcile retry, local-only handling, and publish-state recording. Add or update focused tests showing repeated entry-point calls commit the first dirty batch and then record/return cleanly on the next call without restaging unrelated paths.

steps.description: Invoke artifact publishing from the sprint scheduler after each story reaches a durable terminal state.
steps.details: Add a small runner-local helper that reuses `publish_story_run_audits(_sprint_state, lands_locally=_sprint_lands_locally)` and call it after scheduler-owned terminal audit writes have settled for a story, before the loop can dispatch more ready work. Cover the normal completion path after `_persist_current_story_result` and any `_attempt_integration`/pending-integration drain, plus timeout, worker-exception, auth-cancel, budget-cancel, gate-stand-down, queued-PR resolution, batch-leader propagation, and dropped-story audit paths that can leave canonical run artifacts behind. Leave the existing terminal `publish_story_run_audits` call in place as a final idempotent sweep.

steps.description: Add regression coverage for multi-story project-root landing sprints.
steps.details: Add a two-or-three-story sequential landing regression where the first story writes `.forge/audits/runs/<run_id>.json` and `.forge/knowledge/summaries/<run_id>.yaml`, and assert the publish sequence runs before the next story's entry observes `project_root_dirty_status`. Add/adjust a companion assertion that unrelated project-root dirt is still reported by `landing_precondition_error`, proving the fix commits forge-owned tracked artifacts rather than weakening the gate.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A sprint of N ≥ 2 independent stories, run under a workflow with `on_approve: merge` or `--auto-merge`, completes all N stories without any ESCALATE whose message is the `LANDING PRECONDITION: uncommitted changes` string citing `.forge/audits/runs/` or `.forge/knowledge/summaries/` paths as the dirt.
A precondition refusal caused by genuine operator-introduced dirt unrelated to the canonical run-record or knowledge-summary artifacts must still fire.

risks.description: Parallel sprints can have active workers finishing and writing canonical artifacts while the scheduler publishes a completed story's artifacts.
risks.mitigation: Keep publishing idempotent, scoped only to the two artifact dirs, and retain the terminal sweep so any artifact written during an in-flight publish is committed before sprint exit; avoid holding `phase_lock` around publish.

risks.description: Publishing too early can commit a run record before scheduler-side landing status rewrites it from pending to landed or failed.
risks.mitigation: Place the per-story publish after the scheduler has performed integration/pending-integration drains and rewritten the story audit for the final landing status on that pass.

risks.description: Local-merge runs with `workspace.auto_push` disabled cannot push audit commits without also publishing local story merges.
risks.mitigation: Reuse `_base_branch_tracks_origin` through `publish_story_run_audits` so those commits remain local exactly as today, while still cleaning the working tree for the next landing precondition.
